title: Amazon’s Woot Store Offers Cheap Products
summary: Amazon has opened a new section of its e-commerce empire called Woot, which specializes in selling products at exceptionally low prices. Woot, owned by Amazon, promotes huge discounts on various items, though its inventory is limited and sometimes includes refurbished goods to maintain low prices. The platform aims to capture the bottom end of the market for Amazon.

title: Monolithic Power Systems Gets Price-Target Hikes On Q3 Beat
summary: Monolithic Power Systems (MPWR) exceeded Wall Street's expectations for Q3 earnings and revenue, and provided strong Q4 sales guidance. This led to multiple price target increases from analysts who highlighted strong growth in power management systems for PCs, servers, automotive, and industrial applications. The company has a history of consistently beating sales guidance and is recognized for its product cycle story in the semiconductor industry.

title: Adobe Says Sensei AI Makes Its Software Smarter
summary: Adobe announced Sensei, an array of AI technology being integrated into its software applications for document creation, publishing, and web/mobile performance analysis. Sensei aims to make Adobe's creative and marketing cloud products smarter by leveraging machine learning on trillions of data points gathered from its analytics and image work. Capabilities include advanced document search, context understanding, and intelligent editing features, building on Adobe's domain expertise for specific use cases.

title: NetApp Continues To Layoff Employees
summary: Data storage company NetApp announced another round of layoffs, cutting 6% of its workforce, or about 640 employees. This follows previous job cuts, as the company struggles with the shift to cloud computing. NetApp expects related charges of $50 million to $60 million and hopes its focus on flash storage and hybrid cloud solutions will lead to "moderated growth" by May 2017.

title: Tairen Capital’s Bets on Alibaba Group Holding Ltd (BABA) and Other Tech Stocks Help It Score Big
summary: Tairen Capital achieved a 28.52% return in the third quarter of 2016, largely due to its investment in Alibaba Group Holding Ltd (BABA), where it boosted its stake significantly. The fund also initiated a new position in Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN), which saw a 17% gain. Despite these gains, Tairen Capital was still down over 20% year-to-date, with 62% of its equity portfolio invested in technology stocks.

title: Beware, iPhone Users: Fake Retail Apps Are Surging Before Holidays (Published 2016)
summary: Hundreds of fake retail and product apps have appeared in Apple's App Store, coinciding with the holiday shopping season. These counterfeit apps mimic major retailers and luxury brands, posing risks such as financial fraud, malware infection, and exposure of personal information to unsuspecting iPhone users. Chris Mason, CEO of Branding Brand, noted this surge as unprecedented in a short period.

title: How Iconic Teen Retailer Journeys Has Weathered 30 Years of Changes in Fashion and Business
summary: Jim Estepa, president of Journeys, discusses how the iconic teen retailer has navigated 30 years of retail evolution, fashion shifts, and competition from e-commerce giants like Amazon. The article highlights Journeys' focus on its target demographic, its unique corporate culture, and the role of music in its brand identity. Estepa emphasizes the importance of understanding teen consumers and adapting to their evolving preferences.

title: Eric Schmidt’s Next Book Is About Silicon Valley’s Secret Coach
summary: Alphabet chairman and former Google CEO Eric Schmidt is writing a new book about Bill Campbell, the legendary executive coach who mentored many prominent Silicon Valley figures, including Steve Jobs, Larry Page, Sergey Brin, and Jeff Bezos. Campbell, who passed away in April, was known as the "secret coach" and played a crucial role in Google's organizational structure and growth. This will be Schmidt's third book, following "How Google Works" and "The New Digital Age."

title: Educational Development Corp.: Book publisher's rise to top spot also includes growing pains
summary: Educational Development Corp., a children's book publisher, has rapidly grown its sales and moved into the top spot among public companies in Oklahoma. Despite this success, the company is experiencing growing pains, including significant investments in infrastructure, challenges with direct sales, and managing large inventory due to overseas printing. Moving forward, the company plans for continued expansion, including a partnership with Chick-fil-A, while emphasizing the lasting value of physical books.

title: CareCloud raises $31.5 million in Series C for its cloud health care management platform
summary: CareCloud, a cloud-based healthcare management platform, announced it has raised $31.5 million in Series C financing. The company plans to use the funds to modernize healthcare and address the shifting healthcare marketplace, including increased patient responsibility for costs and potential regulatory changes. CareCloud manages over $4 billion in annualized accounts receivable and aims to be "the single log-in for healthcare."

title: Capital One Cafe Unveils Plans For Southport Store (PHOTOS)
summary: Capital One has revealed plans for its new cafe at 3435 N. Southport Ave. in Chicago's Southport Corridor, expected to open in May or June. The cafe will feature a bank-cafe hybrid concept with Peet's Coffee, financial workshops, and community space, aiming to integrate into the neighborhood's retail district. It will be a two-story, 7,500-square-foot facility with outdoor seating and 24-hour ATM access.

title: Dynatrace to offer SaaS Subscriptions for Cloud Application Monitoring on AWS Marketplace
summary: Dynatrace announced its availability on AWS Marketplace, allowing Amazon Web Services customers to easily purchase and deploy its cloud application performance management service. This integration simplifies procurement and deployment, enabling businesses to quickly troubleshoot and optimize application performance. Dynatrace will demonstrate its solutions at the upcoming re:Invent conference.

title: India’s Parcel shippings grow by 8.2% to 340 mn
summary: India's parcel shipping volumes increased by 8.2% to 340 million, with spending rising by 17.2%, driven by e-commerce growth and modernization among carriers. The market is highly fragmented, with unorganised players constituting 53% of spending, while DTDC is the largest organised player. Globally, the U.S. remains the largest parcel shipping market.

title: Jeff Bezos Invests Billions to Make Amazon a Top E-Commerce Player in India
summary: Jeff Bezos is heavily investing in India to make Amazon a dominant e-commerce player, aiming to avoid a repeat of the company's struggles in China. He has instructed executives to prioritize success in the Indian market, regardless of the cost. Amazon's India presence has rapidly grown from non-existent three years prior to being a strong competitor to local e-commerce leader Flipkart.

title: Ross Stores’ ‘treasure hunt experience’ is its best weapon against Amazon
summary: Ross Stores is leveraging its in-store "treasure hunt experience" to drive traffic and compete effectively against Amazon.com Inc. The off-price retailer reported a 7% increase in same-store sales for the third quarter, with Wedbush analysts noting that over half of this gain was driven by increased customer traffic. This success highlights the relevance of Ross Stores' unique retail model, particularly among millennials, and suggests a strong defense against e-commerce challenges.

title: Salesforce has overcome ‘speed bump,’ analysts say
summary: Analysts are advising investors to buy Salesforce stock before its fourth-quarter results, remarking that the company has overcome a "speed bump." Salesforce's third-quarter earnings showed a recovery, beating expectations with rising sales and growth in subscription and support revenue following a disappointing second quarter. The company also benefited from strong partnerships with financial firms like PNC Bank and Citigroup Inc., and retailers including Amazon.com Inc.

title: Oracle Just Bought Dyn, the Company That Brought Down the Internet
summary: Oracle has acquired Dyn, the internet infrastructure company that was the target of a massive denial-of-service attack last month that temporarily disrupted access to major websites. This acquisition helps Oracle bolster its cloud computing offerings, competing with Amazon and Google by integrating Dyn's DNS services and valuable internet performance data. Dyn's expertise in network intelligence and understanding of internet outages could provide Oracle with a competitive edge in the crowded cloud market.

title: Amazon in Talks to Buy Dubai’s Souq.com in $1 Billion Deal
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is reportedly in discussions to acquire Dubai-based online retailer Souq.com FZ for approximately $1 billion. This potential deal would provide Amazon with a significant entry into the rapidly expanding Middle Eastern e-commerce market. The negotiations are ongoing, and a final agreement has not yet been reached.

title: Allstate to Pay $1.4 Billion for SquareTrade, Seller of Warranties for Mobile Devices, Appliances
summary: Allstate Corp. has agreed to acquire SquareTrade, a provider of protection plans for consumer electronics and appliances, for approximately $1.4 billion. The acquisition aims to enhance Allstate's consumer-focused strategy and expand its customer reach through SquareTrade's strong retail relationships. SquareTrade, which has been growing rapidly and is profitable, will gain broader capabilities with Allstate to expand into new markets and products.

title: Bed Bath & Beyond snaps up PersonalizationMall for $190M
summary: Bed Bath & Beyond has acquired e-commerce site PersonalizationMall for $190 million in cash, aiming to boost its product personalization assortment and fiscal 2016 earnings. This strategic move is intended to help the retailer recapture market share and offer unique gift options amidst slipping sales and challenges from online competition. The acquisition comes as Bed Bath & Beyond attempts to address declining margins and increase its appeal beyond basic home goods.

title: Insurer Allstate to buy SquareTrade for $1.4 billion
summary: Allstate Corp. announced its intent to acquire SquareTrade Holding Co Inc. for approximately $1.4 billion from a group of shareholders including Bain Capital. SquareTrade, founded in 1999, specializes in extended warranty plans for electronic gadgets. This acquisition is expected to help Allstate expand into new markets and products, though it is anticipated to dilute Allstate's earnings per share for three years.

title: FedEx Focuses on Boxes, Marks Cyber Monday Peak
summary: FedEx's national packaging lab plays a crucial role in ensuring products are shipped safely, particularly during the peak holiday season. Technicians at the lab rigorously test packaging for durability to prevent damage and costly returns. Cyber Monday is highlighted as a major peak for package volume, with FedEx expecting to handle record numbers of shipments.

title: CIO Voices: Capital One’s Rob Alexander on How to Win in Banking
summary: Rob Alexander, CIO of Capital One Financial Corp., discusses how technology is reshaping the banking industry and how Capital One is integrating banking services into customers' lives, notably through services like Amazon Alexa. He highlights the company's significant digital transformation project, including a migration to Amazon's cloud and Agile development, to meet evolving customer expectations. Alexander explains how Capital One differentiates itself by offering advanced natural language processing capabilities for banking transactions.

title: Finally! You can now download Netflix shows and movies to watch offline on your phone
summary: Netflix subscribers can now download shows and movies to watch offline at no additional charge. This feature, announced in November 2016, allows users to enjoy content during flights or in areas with limited internet access, a capability already offered by rival Amazon. The company, Netflix Inc., based in Los Gatos, California, stated more downloadable content would be added.

title: Report: Chain negotiating to buy Price Chopper supermarkets
summary: Albertsons Companies Inc. is reportedly in advanced talks to acquire Price Chopper for approximately $1 billion. This potential purchase comes as Price Chopper's owner, Golub Corp., had previously announced plans to convert its stores to the Market 32 brand and invest $300 million. The deal reflects a trend of consolidation in the U.S. grocery industry amidst increasing competition from online retailers and big-box stores.

title: Expedia Turns to Amazon Alexa for Its First Attempt at Voice Search
summary: Expedia has launched its first voice-activated search product on Amazon Alexa, allowing customers to check flight reservations and book car rentals. While full flight and hotel bookings are not yet available, this move signifies Expedia's entry into voice search leveraging its natural language processing efforts. The company believes that testing new platforms like Alexa is crucial as consumers increasingly adopt such technologies.
